questions.q: In a Vernier calipers, when both jaws touch each other, zero of the Vernier scale is shifted to the right of zero of the main scale and $7^{\text{th}}$ Vernier division coincides with a main scale reading. If the value of $1$ main scale division is $1$ mm and there are $10$ Vernier scale divisions, then the Vernier caliper has
questions.solution:
Least count of the Vernier calipers is given by $\text{LC} = \dfrac{1 \text{ MSD}}{\text{Number of VSD}}$.

Substituting the given values, $\text{LC} = \dfrac{1 \text{ mm}}{10} = 0.1 \text{ mm} = 0.01 \text{ cm}$.

Since the zero of the Vernier scale is shifted to the right of the zero of the main scale, the zero error is positive.

The zero error is calculated as $+ (n \times \text{LC})$, where $n$ is the coinciding Vernier division.

Given that the $7^{\text{th}}$ Vernier division coincides with a main scale reading, $n = 7$.

Zero error $= + (7 \times 0.01 \text{ cm}) = + 0.07 \text{ cm}$.

Therefore, the Vernier caliper has a $0.07 \text{ cm}$ positive zero error.

Answer: $0.07$ cm positive zero error

questions.q: In a screw gauge when the circular scale is given five complete rotations it moves linearly by $2.5$ mm. If the circular scale has $100$ divisions, the least count of screw gauge is _____ mm.
questions.solution:
Pitch of the screw gauge is the linear distance moved in one complete rotation.

$\text{Pitch} = \dfrac{2.5}{5} = 0.5 \text{ mm}$

Least count of the screw gauge is given by the ratio of the pitch to the total number of divisions on the circular scale.

$\text{Least count} = \dfrac{\text{Pitch}}{\text{Number of divisions on circular scale}}$

$\text{Least count} = \dfrac{0.5}{100} = 0.005 \text{ mm}$

$\text{Least count} = 5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mm}$

Answer: $5 \times 10^{-3}$

questions.q: In a screw gauge the zero of main scale reference line coincides with the fifth division of the circular scale when two studs are in contact. There are $100$ divisions in circular scale and pitch of screw gauge is $0.1$ mm. When diameter of a sphere is measured, the reading of main scale is $5$ mm and $50^{\text{th}}$ division of circular scale coincides with the reference line of main scale. The diameter of sphere is _______ mm.
questions.solution:
Least count of the screw gauge is given by:

$\text{LC} = \dfrac{\text{Pitch}}{\text{Number of divisions on circular scale}}$

$\text{LC} = \dfrac{0.1}{100} = 0.001 \text{ mm}$

When the two studs are in contact, the $5^{\text{th}}$ division of the circular scale coincides with the reference line. This indicates a positive zero error.

$\text{Zero error} = +5 \times \text{LC} = +5 \times 0.001 = +0.005 \text{ mm}$

For the measurement of the sphere's diameter:

$\text{Main scale reading (MSR)} = 5 \text{ mm}$

$\text{Circular scale reading (CSR)} = 50$

$\text{Measured diameter} = \text{MSR} + \text{CSR} \times \text{LC}$

$\text{Measured diameter} = 5 + 50 \times 0.001 = 5.050 \text{ mm}$

The true diameter is obtained by subtracting the zero error from the measured value:

$\text{True diameter} = \text{Measured diameter} - \text{Zero error}$

$\text{True diameter} = 5.050 - 0.005 = 5.045 \text{ mm}$

Answer: $5.045$

questions.solution:
Least count is the smallest division readable on an instrument scale.
Given readings are 1.24 mm, 1.25 mm, 1.23 mm, 1.21 mm, all expressed to two decimal places.
The precision of measurement shows differences as small as 0.01 mm (e.g., 1.25 - 1.24 = 0.01 mm).
This indicates all readings can be recorded to the nearest 0.01 mm, which represents the smallest measurable division.
Therefore, the least count of the instrument is 0.01 mm.

questions.q:
When both jaws of vernier callipers touch each other, zero mark of the vernier scale is right to zero mark of main scale, $4^{\text{th }}$ mark on vernier scale coincides with certain mark on the main scale. While measuring the length of a cylinder, observer observes 15 divisions on main scale and $5^{\text{th }}$ division of vernier scale coincides with a main scale division. Measured length of cylinder is $\_\_\_\_$ mm.
(Least count of Vernier calliper $=0.1 \mathrm{ mm} )$
questions.solution:
Given Least Count ($LC$) = $0.1$ mm.
When jaws touch, the zero of the vernier scale is to the right of the main scale zero, indicating a positive zero error.
Zero error ($e$) = $+ (n \times LC)$, where $n$ is the coinciding vernier division.
$e = +(4 \times 0.1) = +0.4$ mm.
While measuring the cylinder:
Main Scale Reading ($MSR$) = $15$ divisions.
Assuming $1$ MSD = $1$ mm (standard for $LC = 0.1$ mm), $MSR = 15$ mm.
Vernier Scale Reading ($VSR$) = $5 \times LC = 5 \times 0.1 = 0.5$ mm.
Observed Reading = $MSR + VSR = 15 + 0.5 = 15.5$ mm.
True Measured Length = Observed Reading $-$ Zero Error
True Length = $15.5 - 0.4 = 15.1$ mm.

Least count = 1 main division - 1 vernier division = 0.05 - 0.048 = 0.002 mm

questions.q:
In a screw gauge, the zero of the circular scale lies 3 divisions above the horizontal pitch line when their metallic studs are brought in contact. Using this instrument thickness of a sheet is measured. If pitch scale reading is 1 mm and the circular scale reading is 51 then the correct thickness of the sheet is $\_\_\_\_$ mm.
[Assume least count is 0.01 mm ]
questions.solution:
For a screw gauge, the measurement formula is: Reading = Pitch scale + (Circular scale × Least count) - Zero error
The zero of circular scale lies 3 divisions above the pitch line, indicating negative zero error:
Zero error = -3 × 0.01 = -0.03 mm
Reading = 1 + (51 × 0.01) - (-0.03) = 1 + 0.51 + 0.03 = 1.54 mm

Using a specially designed screw gauge which has pitch of 0.75 mm and 15 divisions in the circular scale, you are asked to find the area of the sheet. questions.q: The least count of a screw guage is 0.01 mm . If the pitch is increased by $75 \%$ and number of divisions on the circular scale is reduced by $50 \%$, the new least count will be _____ $\times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~mm}$

questions.q: One main scale division of a vernier caliper is equal to $m$ units. If $\mathrm{n}^{\text{th }}$ division of main scale coincides with $(n+1)^{\text{th }}$ division of vernier scale, the least count of the vernier caliper is :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{n} M S D=(\mathrm{n}+1) \mathrm{VSD} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 \mathrm{VSD}=\frac{\mathrm{n}}{\mathrm{n}+1} \mathrm{MSD} \\ & \mathrm{L} \cdot \mathrm{C}=1 \mathrm{MSD}-1 \mathrm{VSD} \\ & \mathrm{L} \cdot \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{m}-\mathrm{m}\left(\frac{\mathrm{n}}{\mathrm{n}+1}\right) \\ & \mathrm{L} \cdot \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{m}\left(\frac{\mathrm{n}+1-\mathrm{n}}{\mathrm{n}+1}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{L} \cdot \mathrm{C}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{n}+1}\right)\end{aligned}$

Time period of a simple pendulum is given by, $T = 2\pi\left(\dfrac{l}{g}\right)$.

$= \dfrac{1 . 2}{20}$

Assertion (A) : In Vernier calliper if positive zero error exists, then while taking measurements, the reading taken will be more than the actual reading.

Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
If a positive zero error exists in a vernier callipers, it means that the instrument shows a reading greater than zero even when the jaws are closed and there is no object being measured. In such a case, when actual measurements are taken, the readings will be more than the actual values.

The zero error in Vernier callipers can indeed occur due to manufacturing defects or rough handling. Manufacturing defects may lead to misalignments or inaccuracies in the instrument, while rough handling can result in damage that affects the calibration of the callipers.

Hence, both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

The diameter of the bob will be _____ ${10}^{- 2}cm$.
questions.explanation:
Given,

$1MSD = 1mm$

$10VSD = 9MSD$

Then, $1VSD = \dfrac{9}{10}MSD = 0 . 9MSD$

Least count of Vernier calliper is L.C. $= 0 . 1mm = 0 . 01cm$

Positive zero error$= 0 . 4mm$= 0 . 04cm$

Observed reading of diameter of spherical bob$= 4 . 1cm + 6 \times 0 . 01 = 4 . 16cm$

Real reading of diameter of bob$= 4 . 16 - 0 . 04 = 4 . 12cm$= 412 \times {10}^{- 2}cm$

And $9M . S . D = 10V . S . D$

Reading$= 3 + 6 \times 0 . 01 - \left[- 0 . 06\right]$

Reading$= 3 + 0 . 06 + 0 . 06$

Reading$= 3 . 12cm$

A screw gauge of pitch $0 . 5mm$ is used to measure the diameter of uniform wire of length $6 . 8cm$, the main scale reading is $1 . 5mm$ and circular scale reading is $7$. The calculated curved surface area of wire to appropriate significant figures is
[Screw gauge has $50$ divisions on the circular scale]

$= 3 . 14 \times 6 . 8 \times 1 . 57 \times {10}^{- 1}{cm}^{2}$

$= 3 . 352{cm}^{2} = 3 . 4{cm}^{2}$

questions.q: A student in the laboratory measures thickness of a wire using screw gauge. The readings are $1 . 22mm, 1 . 23mm, 1 . 19mm$ and $1 . 20mm$. The percentage error is $\dfrac{x}{121} %$. The value of $x$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
The average value of the readings is ${x}_{avg} = \dfrac{1 . 19 + 1 . 20 + 1 . 22 + 1 . 23}{4} = 1 . 21$

Now, absolute error in measurement $\Delta{x}_{avg} = \dfrac{0 . 02 + 0 . 01 + 0 . 01 + 0 . 02}{4} = \dfrac{0 . 06}{4} = 0 . 015$

Percentage error in measurement is $= \dfrac{0 . 015}{1 . 21} \times 100 %$= \dfrac{150}{121} %$

So, the value of $x = 150$.

questions.q: A travelling microscope is used to determine the refractive index of a glass slab. If 40 divisions are there in $1cm$ on main scale and $50$ Vernier scale divisions are equal to $49$ main scale divisions, then least count of the travelling microscope is _____ $\times {10}^{- 6}m$.
questions.solution:
Given here, main scale reading, $MS = \dfrac{1}{40}cm$

And, $50 \times VS = 49 \times MS$

Least count of travelling microscope is $LC = MS - VS$

$= MS - \dfrac{49}{50}MS$

$= \dfrac{1}{50} \times MS$

$= \dfrac{1}{50} \times \dfrac{1}{40}cm = \dfrac{1}{2000} \times {10}^{- 2}m$

$= 5 \times {10}^{- 6}m$

questions.solution:
Vernier constant is defined as the difference between the value of one main scale division and one vernier scale division. It is also known as the least count of vernier calliper.

questions.q: In a meter bridge, the wire of length $1m$ has a non-uniform cross-section such that, the variation $\dfrac{dR}{dl}$ of its resistance $R$ with length $l$ is $\dfrac{dR}{dl} ∝ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{l}} .$ Two equal resistances are connected as shown in the figure. The galvanometer has zero deflection when the jockey is at point $P .$ What is the length $AP ?$
questions.solution:
According to question meter bridge have non-uniform wire, where its resistance has a variation with length as $\dfrac{dR}{dl} ∝ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{l}}$

$\dfrac{dR}{dl} = \dfrac{k}{\sqrt{l}} . . . \left(1\right)$

, where $k$ is proportionality constant
Let resistance of the left part $AP$ and right part $PB$ of the wire is ${R}_{AP}, {R}_{PB}$ respectively.

From balanced condition of wheat stone bridge is:

$\dfrac{P}{Q} = \dfrac{R}{S}$

So, from the above condition for given meter bridge is

$\dfrac{{R}^{'}}{{R}^{'}} = \dfrac{{R}_{Ap}}{{R}_{pB}} ⇒ {R}_{Ap} = {R}_{pB} . . . \left(2\right)$

Now from equation $\left(1\right)$, on integrating $∫ dR = k ∫ \dfrac{dl}{\sqrt{l}} . . . \left(3\right)$

for $AP$ part of the wire of length extends from $o$ to $l$ from the equation $\left(3\right)$

${R}_{AP} = {∫}_{0}^{{R}_{AP}} ∫ dR = k{∫}_{0}^{l}\dfrac{dl}{\sqrt{l}} = k{∫}_{0}^{l}\left({l}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}\right)dl = k{\left[{l}^{- \dfrac{1}{2} + 1}\right]}_{0}^{l}- \dfrac{1}{2} + 1 ⇒ {R}_{AP} = 2k\sqrt{l}$

Now, for $PB$ part of the wire of length extends from $l$ to $1m$, from the equation $\left(3\right)$

${R}_{PB} = {∫}_{0}^{{R}_{PB}}dR = k{∫}_{l}^{1}\dfrac{dl}{\sqrt{l}} = k{∫}_{l}^{1}\left({l}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}\right)dl = k{\left[{l}^{- \dfrac{1}{2} + 1}\right]}_{l}^{1}- \dfrac{1}{2} + 1 ⇒ {R}_{PB} = 2k\left[1 - \sqrt{l}\right]$

From equation $\left(2\right)${R}_{AP} = {R}_{PB}$
$∴ 2\sqrt{l} = 2\left(1 - \sqrt{l}\right) ⇒ \sqrt{l} = 1 - \sqrt{l} ⇒ \sqrt{l} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ l = \dfrac{1}{4} = 0 . 25m$

questions.q: In the experimental set up of metre bridge shown in the figure, the null point is obtaine data distance of $40 \mathrm{~cm}$ from A. If a $10 \Omega$ resistor is connected in series with $\mathrm{R}_{1},$ the null point shifts by $10 \mathrm{~cm}$. questions.solution:
Initially at null deflection $\frac{\mathrm{R}_{1}}{\mathrm{R}_{2}}=\frac{2}{3}$\ldots(\mathrm{i})$

Finally at null deflection, when null point is shifted $\frac{\mathrm{R}_{1}+10}{\mathrm{R}_{2}}=1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_{1}+10=\mathrm{R}_{2}$...(ii)

Now if required resistance is $\mathrm{R}$ then $\frac{\frac{30 \times \mathrm{R}}{30+\mathrm{R}}}{30}=\frac{2}{3}$\mathrm{R}=60 \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A screw gauge gives the following reading when used to measure the diameter of a wire.
Main scale reading : $0 \mathrm{~mm}$
Circular scale reading : 52 divisions
Given that $1 \mathrm{~mm}$ on main scale corresponds to 100 divisions of the circular scale.
The diameter of wire from the above date is :
questions.solution: Diameter of wire $=\frac{1}{100} \times 52=0.52 \mathrm{~mm}=0.052 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: In an experiment the angles are required to be measured using an instrument. 29 divisions of the main scale exactly coincide with the 30 divisions of the vernier scale. If the smallest division of the main scale is half-a-degree $\left(=0.5^{\circ}\right)$, then the least count of the instrument is
options:
one minute

half minute

one degree

half degree
questions.solution: $\text{ Least count }=\frac{\text{ value of main scale division }}{\text{ No of divisions on vernier scale }}=\frac{1}{30} \mathrm{MSD}=\frac{1}{30} \times \frac{1}{2}^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{1}{60}^{{}^{\circ}}=$1 $\text{ minute }$

questions.q: Two full turns of the circular scale of a screw gauge cover a distance of $1 \mathrm{~mm}$ on its main scale. The total number of divisions on the circular scale is 50 . Further, it is found that the screw gauge has a zero error of $-0.03 \mathrm{~mm}$ while measuring the diameter of a thin wire, a student notes the main scale reading of $3 \mathrm{~mm}$ and the number of circular scale divisions in line with the main scale as 35 . The diameter of the wire is
questions.solution: Diameter $=$ M.S.R. $+$ C.S.R $\times$ L.C. $+$ Z.E. $=3+35 \times(0.5 / 50)+0.03=3.38 \mathrm{~mm}$
